title: Frassati the Dominican
hook: Pier Giorgio was a lay Dominican

segments.voice: Yesterday, lay Dominicans: people with jobs and families who promise to pray, study and share where they already stand. Your line was lay preachers. Did you ask someone to read one short thing with you? Day one thousand two hundred forty-four.

An old black-and-white photograph. A young man in a hat and climbing gear, on a steep slope of rock, roped, leaning into the climb. Across the bottom of the photo, in his own handwriting, a short Italian phrase: verso l'alto. Toward the top. He was a student in Turin from a well-known family, the kind of young man who could have spent his life comfortably. Friends remembered him as loud, funny, a practical joker, quick to suggest a hike. And quietly, on his own, he had joined yesterday's people. Pier Giorgio Frassati was a lay Dominican. Today's word is the climber who was quietly a Dominican.
screen: `A PHOTO ON A ROCK FACE.` → `HIS OWN WORDS: VERSO L'ALTO.` → `A LAY DOMINICAN IN CLIMBING GEAR.`

segments.voice: When Pier Giorgio made his promise as a lay Dominican, he took a new name in the order: Girolamo, Jerome. He kept his ordinary life. He studied engineering, argued politics, went to Mass, and dragged his friends up mountains. But the Dominican three, pray, study, share, ran underneath all of it. The sharing is the part his own family didn't see. He visited the poor of Turin, by his friends' accounts, bringing food, paying for medicine, giving away what he had, sometimes even his fare home, so that he walked. He didn't announce it. When he died young, after a sudden illness, the story told about his funeral is that the streets filled with poor people his parents had never met, people he had been visiting all along. That is a lay preacher's sermon: preached without a pulpit, and heard only at the end. And the mountains? For him they weren't a break from faith. They were part of it. The Psalms in the Douay-Rheims say: "I have lifted up my eyes to the mountains, from whence help shall come to me." Climbing, for Pier Giorgio, was a way of going toward God with your whole body, roped to a friend, step by step. Verso l'alto. Toward the top, and never alone on the rope. The Church holds him up as a model for young people, and his phrase has become a kind of motto: not a call to be grim or perfect, but to keep climbing, with friends, toward the summit.
screen: `A NEW NAME: GIROLAMO.` · `HE GAVE AWAY EVEN HIS FARE HOME.` · `A FUNERAL FULL OF STRANGERS.` · `THE MOUNTAIN WAS PART OF THE PRAYER.` · then, large: `VERSO L'ALTO.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: climb, or walk, with a friend. Right now, if you can, stand up and take a few slow steps, or simply lift your eyes to the highest thing you can see: a ceiling, a treetop, a hill out the window. Breathe there. Then bring to mind one friend you could walk with this week, up a hill, a staircase, or just around the block. Name them. Hold the picture of the two of you moving uphill together. If you pray, you can lift your eyes to the mountains, as the psalm says. The bell holds the time.
Frassati the Dominican. Pier Giorgio, a student and climber in Turin who joined the lay Dominicans and served the poor so quietly his family found out at his funeral. Today's word.

Your line: verso l'alto. Toward the top. Today, when a climb comes, a staircase, a hill, a hard task, take it on purpose, and if you can, take it with that friend. Day one thousand two hundred forty-four.

howItsDone: Some young Catholics in parish and campus groups take Pier Giorgio Frassati as a patron, and some organize hikes and climbs under his motto, verso l'alto.

notes: Claims rule: no dates or ages in the voice. 'Died young, after a sudden illness' (polio) kept general.
Confirm: Frassati joined the Dominican laity and took the name Girolamo (after Savonarola, not mentioned in the voice); wrote 'verso l'alto' on a climbing photograph.
The bus-fare story and the funeral crowd of the poor are biographical traditions; hedged as 'by his friends' accounts' and 'the story told'. Confirm.
Status: Frassati was beatified by John Paul II and canonized (2025). The voice says only 'the Church holds him up as a model for young people'; a Keeper may want 'Saint Pier Giorgio' added.
'Studied engineering' (mining engineering at the Turin Polytechnic): confirm.
